Building an "award-winning" 3D/scroll-driven portfolio site for Rafael Costa (Founder & Product Analyst, Lisbon — data/analytics work across Meridian Bank, Helix Genomics Institute, Atlantico Telecom, and his own projects DataTugas/FraudShield/AutoPilot/Lisbon Rent Map).

Agreed concept (plan delivered 2026-10-10, not yet built): "signal from noise" — site opens in visual chaos (scattered data points in 3D) that resolves into order section by section, mirroring Rafael's actual throughline of turning operational chaos into tools non-analysts can use. One continuous scroll-driven camera move through a single 3D scene rather than stacked template sections. Palette: near-black + off-white, terracotta/amber accent + signal teal accent, no more. Mobile drops pinned 3D camera scrubbing in favor of lighter pre-baked animations with the same visual idea.

**Why:** user explicitly rejected a generic template/demo feel and wants the site to "feel like me and my work" — the 3D has to carry narrative meaning (his actual pattern of work), not be decorative.

**Open items blocking build** — found via `material/resume.md` vs `material/linkedin-export/*.csv` discrepancies:
- Reporting-time-reduced stat: resume says 40%, LinkedIn says 60% (unresolved)
- Lisbon Rent Map traffic: resume says 5,000/mo, LinkedIn says 3,000/mo (unresolved)
- MSc Data Science end date: resume says 2021, LinkedIn says 2022 (unresolved)
- Resume email is a placeholder (rafael@example.com) — need real contact info
- No real dashboard screenshots likely available (bank/genomics confidentiality) — may need sanitized mockups or lean fully on abstract 3D visuals instead

**How to apply:** before writing any content/copy for the site, confirm these numbers and contact info with the user rather than picking one source. Don't start building until user responds to the plan in the prior turn.

content.text:
Understood — no more questions. I made the calls myself and locked them in. Here's the complete, decided plan:

## Judgment calls I made (so nothing's hidden, but nothing's blocking)

- **Reporting-time stat (Helix Genomics):** going with the resume's **40%**, not LinkedIn's 60% — lower, more defensible number for a public claim.
- **Lisbon Rent Map traffic:** going with **3,000 visitors/mo** (the lower of the two) for the same reason.
- **MSc Data Science dates:** going with **2020–2022** (LinkedIn) — matches the standard 2-year length for the degree, more plausible than a 1-year run.
- **Contact:** resume email is a placeholder, so the site ships with a styled contact form instead of a raw mailto — no real inbox needed to launch, swap in a forwarding address whenever you want.
- **Case study visuals:** assuming no releasable Meridian Bank / Helix Genomics screenshots exist (confidentiality). Both case studies run entirely on the abstract 3D motif (dashboard assembling, strands combing straight) rather than real UI — this also means they age well since there's nothing to update.

## The idea

**Signal from noise.** Across Meridian Bank, Helix Genomics, Atlantico, and your own projects, the actual pattern is: you walk into operational chaos and leave behind something a non-analyst can run without you. The site makes that literal — it opens in visual disorder (scattered points, numbers, fragments in 3D) and each section is the moment one piece of that chaos resolves into something ordered, mirroring what you actually do. One continuous scroll-driven camera move through a single 3D scene, not stacked template sections.

## The scroll journey

**1. Hero — the noise.** Dark field of drifting, unlabeled data points/digits, no structure. Name + line on top: *"I make dashboards people actually use."* Scrolling drags the camera forward into the field.

**2. The thesis.** Short paragraph on the "chaos in, structure out" pattern, with a quiet stat strip — 3 industries, 200+ staff using what you built, 40% faster reporting. First hint of a grid emerging under the noise.

**3. Meridian Bank.** Problem: no shared visibility across 200+ staff. Chaos resolves into a dashboard panel assembling itself as you scroll — filters snapping in, a chart drawing from scattered points. Close on the 35% efficiency figure.

**4. Helix Genomics.** Problem: sequencer double-booking, slow reporting. Tangled strand motif combs into parallel ordered tracks. Beatriz Lima's quote lands here as a pull-quote. Close on the 40% figure.

**5. Lisbon Rent Map — flagship.** Flat scattered rent listings lift into a 3D extruded map of Lisbon's parishes, height/colour mapped to price. Live link out. Close on 3,000 visitors/mo.

**6. Other work.** FraudShield, AutoPilot, DataTugas, Atlantico churn — a tighter grid, one line + outcome each, same settling-structure visual but smaller and faster, no pinned camera stop.

**7. Toolkit.** SQL, Python, Tableau, Power BI, dbt, Statistics — the last loose particles from the hero snapping into a small cluster, not a badge wall.

**8. Credibility.** Health Data Hackathon win, MSc Data Science (2020–2022) + BSc Economics. Calm, text-forward.

**9. Contact — full stillness.** Noise field now a clean, still grid. Contact form, resume download, social links — mirrors the hero, closes the arc.

## Colour and type

- **Base:** near-black ink background, off-white text.
- **Accent 1 (warm):** terracotta/amber — Lisbon tilework nod, used for the Rent Map section and key highlights.
- **Accent 2 (cool):** signal teal — the "resolved" colour, triggered whenever noise snaps into structure.
- Nothing beyond those two accents.
- **Type:** a neutral, technically-credible grotesk (Inter/Söhne territory) for body/UI, paired with a higher-personality display face for scroll-triggered headlines — leaning serif-with-editorial-weight to match the data-journalism feel of the Rent Map and genomics paper. Final face picked at build time once licensing/self-hosting is checked.

## Phone behaviour

- No pinned/scrubbed 3D camera on mobile — each case study becomes a normal vertical scroll with a lighter pre-baked animation standing in for the same visual idea.
- Particle counts in the noise field capped hard on mobile.
- Tested on a real mid-range Android, not just iPhone.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` respected everywhere.

## What the site still needs from you, whenever you have a minute (not blocking)

- A real forwarding address behind the contact form.
- A resume/CV file to link for download.
- 3–4 sentences per case study beyond the one-liners, when you get time — not required to start building.

Ready to start building section by section — say go and I'll begin with the hero and the noise-to-structure system, since everything else inherits from it.
